title: Board Policy on Assessing Security Deposits
content:
## 1. Occasions for an assessment

A Security Deposits deposit is assessed when a service account is opened for new service, when an account is reconnected after a nonpayment disconnection, when usage growth triggers a reassessment, or when a waived account is disconnected for nonpayment.

## 2. Accounts that may be assessed

A deposit may be assessed only on a service account in pending connection, active, disconnect pending or disconnected for nonpayment status. The status is read from the service account record of the account being assessed, before the assessment; an account in any other status is not assessed. A member enrolled in PrePay Power is never assessed a deposit on the prepay meter.

## 3. Choice of tier

The tier is the deposit tier named by the service account's rate schedule, except that a reconnection after a nonpayment disconnection on Schedule R or Schedule FH is assessed on the Residential Credit Reestablishment Deposit. A tier is used only for service accounts on its eligible rate schedules, and only for the assessment bases it lists.

## 4. The basis bill and the history of a location

The basis bill is read from the billing periods of the tier's bill lookback immediately before the assessed date, on the service account being assessed (for a transfer, the location's billing under the same service location's meter). Each billing period's total is the sum of its usage charge lines; the basis bill is the average of those period totals on a tier whose basis is the average bill, and the largest period total on a tier whose basis is the highest bill. The number of billing periods that carry usage charge lines is the location's history length.

## 5. Amount

5.1 *Retired clause.* The clause providing that the amount is the tier's deposit multiple times the basis bill when the location has at least the tier's minimum history, and otherwise the higher of the new-service flat estimate and the estimate per kVA multiplied by the transformer kVA, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

5.2 The result is rounded up to the next multiple of the tier's rounding increment, raised to the tier's minimum deposit when lower, and then limited by the combined ceiling on the service account.

## 6. Installments

When the tier allows installments the member is granted the tier's installment count; otherwise the installment count is 1.

## Points of judgement

| Question | Answer under this policy |
|---|---|
| A Schedule FH account is being reconnected after a nonpayment disconnection. Which tier? | Residential Credit Reestablishment Deposit. |
| A Schedule GS-1 account is being reconnected after a nonpayment disconnection. Which tier? | General Service Deposit, the tier its schedule names, which lists that basis. |
| May a final-billed account be assessed? | No; only the four statuses in section 2 may be. |
| A hypothetical computed amount of $287.40 on the Residential Standard Deposit, whose rounding increment is $5.00 and minimum $100.00: what results before the ceiling? | $290.00, the next multiple of $5.00, already above the minimum. |
| A hypothetical computed amount of $62.10 on the Seasonal Residence Deposit (increment $5.00, minimum $100.00)? | Rounded up to $65.00, then raised to the $100.00 minimum. |

superseded_clauses: The amount is deposit_multiple times the basis bill of deposit_msr_bill_basis when the location has at least min_history_months of history, and otherwise the higher of new_service_estimated_deposit and new_service_estimate_per_kva times the transformer_kva.
